claim: 3DeeCellTracker is a deep learning-based software pipeline for segmenting and tracking cells in 3D time lapse images.
source: We developed a deep learning-based software pipeline, 3DeeCellTracker, by integrating multiple existing and new techniques including deep learning for tracking.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the main contribution of the work.

claim: With only one volume of training data, one initial correction, and a few parameter changes, 3DeeCellTracker successfully segmented and tracked ~100 cells in both semi-immobilized and 'straightened' freely moving worm's brain.
source: With only one volume of training data, one initial correction, and a few parameter changes, 3DeeCellTracker successfully segmented and tracked ~100 cells in both semi-immobilized and 'straightened' freely moving worm's brain, in a naturally beating zebrafish heart, and ~1000 cells in a 3D cultured tumor spheroid.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker successfully tracked cells in a naturally beating zebrafish heart.
source: With only one volume of training data, one initial correction, and a few parameter changes, 3DeeCellTracker successfully segmented and tracked ~100 cells in both semi-immobilized and 'straightened' freely moving worm's brain, in a naturally beating zebrafish heart, and ~1000 cells in a 3D cultured tumor spheroid.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with experimental data in the results section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker successfully tracked ~1000 cells in a 3D cultured tumor spheroid.
source: With only one volume of training data, one initial correction, and a few parameter changes, 3DeeCellTracker successfully segmented and tracked ~100 cells in both semi-immobilized and 'straightened' freely moving worm's brain, in a naturally beating zebrafish heart, and ~1000 cells in a 3D cultured tumor spheroid.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated with experimental data showing tracking of 901 cells in the tumor spheroid dataset.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker tracked 90–100% of the cells in most cases, which is comparable or superior to previous results.
source: While these datasets were imaged with highly divergent optical systems, our method tracked 90–100% of the cells in most cases, which is comparable or superior to previous results.
evidence: This claim is supported by tracking accuracy data presented throughout the results section and comparison with other methods.

claim: Processing cells in 3D + T images has remained difficult, especially when cells cannot be clearly separated and/or their movements are relatively large.
source: However, processing cells in 3D + T images has remained difficult, especially when cells cannot be clearly separated and/or their movements are relatively large, such as cells in deforming organs.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about the challenges in the field.

claim: For processing objects in 3D + T images, two steps are required: segmentation and tracking.
source: For processing objects in 3D + T images, the following two steps are required: (1) segmentation: segmenting the regions of interest in each 3D image into individual objects (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, left) and (2) tracking: linking an object in a particular volume to the same object in the temporally adjacent volume (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, right).
evidence: This is stated as a fundamental requirement for processing 3D + T images.

claim: Programs optimized for processing images in particular conditions have been developed for segmenting and tracking cells of deforming organs in 3D + T images.
source: For segmenting and tracking (hereafter collectively called 'tracking') cells of deforming organs in 3D + T images, programs optimized for processing images in particular conditions have been developed (Schrödel et al., 2013; Toyoshima et al., 2016; Venkatachalam et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work in the field.

claim: Previous methods for tracking cells in 3D + T images cannot be used under conditions other than those for which they were designed, at least without a loss in processing efficiency.
source: However, these methods cannot be used under conditions other than those for which they were designed, at least without a loss in processing efficiency.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of previous methods based on the authors' understanding of the field.

claim: 3D + T images, especially those obtained under challenging conditions, can be efficiently processed only when customized software is developed specifically for those images.
source: In other words, 3D + T images, especially those obtained under challenging conditions, can be efficiently processed only when customized software is developed specifically for those images.
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the limitations of previous methods.

claim: Changes in lighting could require the re-optimization of parameters for segmentation and tracking in 2D image processing.
source: For example, even in 2D image processing, changes in lighting could require the re-optimization of parameters for segmentation and tracking (Egnor and Branson, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Deep learning methods use an artificial neural network with multiple layers to process complex data and automatically optimize a number of parameters from training data.
source: Deep learning methods use an artificial neural network with multiple layers, that is, a deep network, to process complex data and automatically optimize a number of parameters from training data, which allows users to easily apply a single method to images obtained under different conditions.
evidence: This is a description of deep learning methods based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Deep learning methods have outperformed conventional methods in some image processing tasks such as image classification.
source: In addition to this flexibility, deep learning methods have outperformed conventional methods in some image processing tasks such as image classification (LeCun et al., 2015; Krizhevsky et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work demonstrating the superiority of deep learning in certain tasks.

claim: Deep learning methods are used mostly for segmentation and/or object detection, but not for tracking because of the difficulty in preparing training data.
source: Nevertheless, deep learning methods are used mostly for segmentation and/or object detection, but not for tracking because of the difficulty in preparing training data (Moen et al., 2019): Correctly tracking a number of objects manually to obtain training data, especially from 3D + T images recorded over long period of time, is extremely challenging.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of applying deep learning to tracking, supported by a citation.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker is a new pipeline utilizing deep learning techniques in segmentation and, for the first time to the authors' knowledge, in tracking of cells in 3D + T images.
source: In this study, we developed 3DeeCellTracker, a new pipeline utilizing deep learning techniques in segmentation and, for the first time to our knowledge, in tracking of cells in 3D + T images.
evidence: This is stated as a key contribution of the work.

claim: The problem of training data preparation for tracking was solved by creating a synthetic dataset.
source: We solved the problem of training data preparation for tracking by creating a synthetic dataset (see below).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological innovation and is described in detail in the methods section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker was implemented on a desktop PC to efficiently and flexibly track cells over hundreds of volumes of 3D + T images recorded under highly divergent optical or imaging conditions.
source: 3DeeCellTracker was implemented on a desktop PC to efficiently and flexibly track cells over hundreds of volumes of 3D + T images recorded under highly divergent optical or imaging conditions.
evidence: This is stated as a feature of the method and demonstrated through the various datasets analyzed.

claim: Using only one volume for training and one initial correction, 3DeeCellTracker efficiently tracked 100–150 neurons in the brains of semi-immobilized or 'straightened' freely moving Caenorhabditis elegans roundworms from four image datasets.
source: Using only one volume for training and one initial correction, 3DeeCellTracker efficiently tracked 100–150 neurons in the brains of semi-immobilized or 'straightened' (special pre-processing step based on the worm's posture) freely moving Caenorhabditis elegans roundworms from four image datasets, obtained using spinning disk confocal systems in three different laboratories.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experimental results in the results section.

claim: The four worm datasets were obtained using spinning disk confocal systems in three different laboratories.
source: Using only one volume for training and one initial correction, 3DeeCellTracker efficiently tracked 100–150 neurons in the brains of semi-immobilized or 'straightened' (special pre-processing step based on the worm's posture) freely moving Caenorhabditis elegans roundworms from four image datasets, obtained using spinning disk confocal systems in three different laboratories.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and details are provided in the materials and methods section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker tracked ~100 cells in the naturally beating heart of a zebrafish larva monitored using swept confocally aligned planar excitation (SCAPE) microscopy.
source: With a few modifications, 3DeeCellTracker also tracked ~100 cells in the naturally beating heart of a zebrafish larva monitored using swept confocally aligned planar excitation (SCAPE) microscopy, a novel oblique light sheet microscope system for very rapid 3D + T imaging (Bouchard et al., 2015; Voleti et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in the results section.

claim: SCAPE microscopy is a novel oblique light sheet microscope system for very rapid 3D + T imaging.
source: With a few modifications, 3DeeCellTracker also tracked ~100 cells in the naturally beating heart of a zebrafish larva monitored using swept confocally aligned planar excitation (SCAPE) microscopy, a novel oblique light sheet microscope system for very rapid 3D + T imaging (Bouchard et al., 2015; Voleti et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work describing the SCAPE system.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker tracked ~900 cells in a cultured 3D tumor spheroid, which were imaged with a two photon microscope system.
source: Furthermore, 3DeeCellTracker tracked ~900 cells in a cultured 3D tumor spheroid, which were imaged with a two photon microscope system.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in the results section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker provided robust tracking results from real datasets as well as from degenerated datasets, which differed in terms of signal-to-noise ratios, cell movements, and resolutions along the z-axis.
source: Our pipeline provided robust tracking results from the above-mentioned real datasets as well as from degenerated datasets, which differed in terms of signal-to-noise ratios, cell movements, and resolutions along the z-axis.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in the results section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker's performance was better in terms of the tracking results than those from recently developed 2D/3D tracking software running on a desktop PC.
source: Notably, 3DeeCellTracker's performance was better in terms of the tracking results than those from recently developed 2D/3D tracking software running on a desktop PC, and comparable to software running on ﻿a high-performance computing cluster (Toyoshima et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2017; Bannon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by comparison data in the results section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker's performance was comparable to software running on a high-performance computing cluster.
source: Notably, 3DeeCellTracker's performance was better in terms of the tracking results than those from recently developed 2D/3D tracking software running on a desktop PC, and comparable to software running on ﻿a high-performance computing cluster (Toyoshima et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2017; Bannon et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by comparison data in the results section.

claim: The worm's neurons exhibited complex activity patterns in the brain.
source: Furthermore, by using the positional information of the tracked cells, we extracted dynamics of the cells: the worm's neurons exhibited complex activity patterns in the brain, the zebrafish heart cells exhibited activities synchronized with heart chamber movement, and the tumor spheroid cells exhibited spontaneous activities without stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated with extracted activity data in the results section.

claim: The zebrafish heart cells exhibited activities synchronized with heart chamber movement.
source: Furthermore, by using the positional information of the tracked cells, we extracted dynamics of the cells: the worm's neurons exhibited complex activity patterns in the brain, the zebrafish heart cells exhibited activities synchronized with heart chamber movement, and the tumor spheroid cells exhibited spontaneous activities without stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated with extracted activity data in the results section.

claim: The tumor spheroid cells exhibited spontaneous activities without stimulation.
source: Furthermore, by using the positional information of the tracked cells, we extracted dynamics of the cells: the worm's neurons exhibited complex activity patterns in the brain, the zebrafish heart cells exhibited activities synchronized with heart chamber movement, and the tumor spheroid cells exhibited spontaneous activities without stimulation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated with extracted activity data in the results section.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker integrates novel and existing techniques.
source: We developed a new pipeline, 3DeeCellTracker, which integrates novel and existing techniques (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the overview section of the results.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker performs automatic segmentation of cells in all 3D + T images using 3D U-Net.
source: After preprocessing (see Materials and methods), it performs automatic segmentation of cells in all 3D + T images using 3D U-Net for classifying individual voxels into cell or non-cell categories (Ronneberger et al., 2015; Çiçek et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the overview section and described in detail in the methods.

claim: 3D U-Net classifies individual voxels into cell or non-cell categories.
source: After preprocessing (see Materials and methods), it performs automatic segmentation of cells in all 3D + T images using 3D U-Net for classifying individual voxels into cell or non-cell categories (Ronneberger et al., 2015; Çiçek et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the overview section with citations to the original U-Net papers.

claim: Continuous regions of 'cell' voxels are separated into individual cell regions using the watershed method.
source: Continuous regions of 'cell' voxels are separated into individual cell regions using the watershed method (Beucher and Meyer, 1993), and then numbered.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section with a citation to the watershed method.

claim: The segmented cells are manually corrected only in the first volume of 3D images.
source: The segmented cells are manually corrected only in the first volume of 3D images.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section as part of the pipeline procedure.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker uses a feedforward network (FFN) to predict cell positions based on spatial patterns of cells maintained between previous and current images.
source: In the following 3D tracking step, we considerably increased the efficiency by introducing a deep learning technique, feedforward network (FFN), to predict cell positions based on spatial patterns of cells maintained between previous and current images.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section as a key innovation of the method.

claim: The predicted positions from FFN are corrected with a non-rigid point set registration method called PR-GLS.
source: The predicted positions are corrected with a non-rigid point set registration method called PR-GLS (Ma et al., 2016) and by our custom method to obtain precise cell locations, which are critical for extracting the accurate dynamics of cellular signals.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section with a citation to the PR-GLS method.

claim: The 3D U-Net is pre-trained using manually confirmed data from a single 3D image volume.
source: The 3D U-Net and the FFN are pre-trained using manually confirmed data or synthetic data (Figure 1B,C) from a single 3D image volume.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section and described in detail in the methods.

claim: The FFN is pre-trained using synthetic data from a single 3D image volume.
source: The 3D U-Net and the FFN are pre-trained using manually confirmed data or synthetic data (Figure 1B,C) from a single 3D image volume.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section and described in detail in the methods.

claim: The keys to the method are the use of simulation to produce large amounts of training data for the FFN and the carefully designed post-processing methods for the FFN.
source: The keys to our method are the use of simulation to produce large amounts of training data for the FFN and the carefully designed post-processing methods for the FFN, which result in the flexible and robust tracking of moving cells in very different 3D + T datasets.
evidence: This is stated in the overview section as the key innovations of the method.

claim: The U-Net can generate precise segmentation under diverse imaging conditions and can be trained with very few annotated images.
source: The U-Net can generate precise segmentation under diverse imaging conditions and can be trained with very few annotated images (e.g. only one 3D image volume in this study; see Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the segmentation section and demonstrated through the experiments.

claim: The pre-processed images of the first volume are used to train the 3D U-Net.
source: The pre-processed images of the first volume are used to train the 3D U-Net (Figure 1B), and the trained U-net is then used for the segmentation of cells in all the following volumes.
evidence: This is stated in the segmentation section as part of the method.

claim: Once trained on one dataset, the 3D U-Net can be directly reused for different datasets obtained under similar optical conditions.
source: Once trained on one dataset, the 3D U-Net can be directly reused for different datasets obtained under similar optical conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the segmentation section as a feature of the method.

claim: FFN matches temporally adjacent cells based on the distance pattern between each cell and its 20 surrounding cells.
source: We used FFN to match temporally adjacent cells based on the distance pattern between each cell and its 20 surrounding cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the tracking section as part of the method.

claim: Deep network techniques had not been used previously for cell tracking because they require large amounts of training data that are difficult to prepare manually.
source: Although deep network techniques are expected to produce superior cell tracking results, the method had not been used previously because it requires large amounts of training data. These data are difficult to prepare manually, especially for 3D + T images, as validating and correcting large numbers of cell positions over time by switching multiple layers along the z axis is virtually impossible.
evidence: This is stated in the tracking section as the motivation for using synthetic data.

claim: More than 500,000,000 synthetic training data points were generated by simulating cell movements.
source: To solve this difficulty in preparing training data for FFN, we generated >500,000,000 synthetic training data points by simulating cell movements (see Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the tracking section and described in detail in the methods.

claim: FFN generates more accurate initial matchings than FPFH.
source: Originally, PR-GLS was used in conjunction with the FPFH method to predict cell positions (Ma et al., 2016); however, our FFN generates more accurate initial matchings than FPFH (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B), and our combination of FFN + PR-GLS generates more accurate predictions of cell positions than the FPFH + PR-GLS or the classic affine alignment (Myronenko et al., 2006) does (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the tracking section and supported by comparison data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The combination of FFN + PR-GLS generates more accurate predictions of cell positions than FPFH + PR-GLS or classic affine alignment.
source: Originally, PR-GLS was used in conjunction with the FPFH method to predict cell positions (Ma et al., 2016); however, our FFN generates more accurate initial matchings than FPFH (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B), and our combination of FFN + PR-GLS generates more accurate predictions of cell positions than the FPFH + PR-GLS or the classic affine alignment (Myronenko et al., 2006) does (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the tracking section and supported by comparison data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The estimated positions from FFN + PR-GLS are accurately corrected to compensate for their differences by utilizing information from local cell regions contained in the 3D U-Net output.
source: To overcome these errors, the estimated positions are accurately corrected to compensate for their differences by utilizing information from local cell regions contained in the 3D U-Net output (Figure 2C, panel 5, Figure 2—figure supplement 4, and Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the tracking section and illustrated in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: C. elegans has been used as a model for imaging all neuronal activities in the brain owing to its small brain, transparent body, complete description of all connections of 302 neurons, feasibility in the use of genetically encoded calcium indicators, and the capability of perception, memory, and decision-making in its small brain.
source: C. elegans has been used as a model for imaging all neuronal activities in the brain ('whole brain imaging') owing to its small brain (~40 µm3 in an adult) in a transparent body, the complete description of all connections of 302 neurons, feasibility in the use of genetically encoded calcium indicators (GECI), and the capability of perception, memory, and decision-making in its small brain (de Bono and Maricq, 2005).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with a citation.

claim: Whole brain imaging of C. elegans has been reported from several laboratories, and the most popular optical system currently is the spinning disk confocal system.
source: Whole brain imaging of C. elegans has been reported from several laboratories, and the most popular optical system currently is the spinning disk confocal system, for which each laboratory has developed their own tracking software (Schrödel et al., 2013; Toyoshima et al., 2016; Venkatachalam et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge with citations to previous work.

claim: In dataset worm #1a, 164 neurons were manually confirmed in the head in the first volume of 3D + T images.
source: After segmentation, we manually confirmed 164 neurons in the head in the first volume of 3D + T images, in which the distribution of cell signals was mostly, but not completely, separated from the background signals (dataset worm #1a; see Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: In dataset worm #1a, the method tracked all the neurons in all 171 volumes except for those that moved out of the field of view of the camera.
source: Our method tracked all the neurons in all 171 volumes except for those that moved out of the field of view of the camera (Figure 3D–F, Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3.

claim: When RM is small, searching for the closest cell is the simplest method to find the new position of a given cell in the next volume.
source: When RM is small, searching for the closest cell is the simplest method to find the new position of a given cell in the next volume.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an explanation of the RM metric.

claim: A simple approach of searching for the closest cell may lead to tracking errors when RM ≥0.5.
source: However, such a simple approach may lead to tracking errors when RM ≥0.5 (Figure 4 and Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and illustrated in Figure 4.

claim: Most of the cell RM values were ≤0.5 in the worm #1 dataset.
source: Although most of the cell RM values were ≤0.5 in the worm #1 dataset (Figure 3B, bottom), other datasets had cells with RM ≥0.5; nevertheless, these were also successfully tracked by our program (see below).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The method achieved 100% tracking accuracy in dataset worm #1b without changing any parameters aside from the noise level.
source: We also tested worm #1b dataset, obtained from the same strain with worm #1a (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), in which we again achieved 100% tracking accuracy without changing any parameters aside from the noise level (see Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Tables 1 and 2.

claim: The method achieved a 100% accuracy of tracking in dataset worm #2.
source: Our method again achieved a 100% accuracy of tracking and extracted calcium signals from all 101 neurons even though this dataset differs considerably from the worm #1 dataset in terms of nuclear marker intensity and movement patterns (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–F, Figure 3—video 2 and Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: More neurons were detected using the method than using the original method in dataset worm #2 (approximately 90 neurons or less).
source: It should be noted that more neurons were detected using our method than using the original method (approximately 90 neurons or less) (Nguyen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to the original study.

claim: In dataset worm #3, the worm was loosely constrained in a microfluidic device and not anesthetized, thus exhibited larger head deformations and cell displacements between volumes (by a factor of approximately three times) compared to the worm #1 and #2 datasets.
source: In this case, the worm was loosely constrained in a microfluidic device and not anesthetized, thus exhibited larger head deformations and cell displacements between volumes (by a factor of approximately three times) compared to the worm #1 and #2 datasets (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Dataset worm #3 had a lower resolution (half the resolution in the x and y directions) compared to worm #1 and #2 datasets.
source: In addition, this dataset had a lower resolution (half the resolution in the x and y directions).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a characteristic of dataset worm #3.

claim: With a few parameter modifications, the method correctly tracked 171/175 (=98%) of the neurons in dataset worm #3.
source: Nevertheless, with a few parameter modifications (Table 2 and Materials and methods), our method correctly tracked 171/175 (=98%) of the neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C–F and Figure 3—video 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3 and Table 2.

claim: The result in dataset worm #3 was comparable to that of the original report, in which 171 out of 198 neurons were tracked without error.
source: Our result was comparable to that of the original report, in which 171 out of 198 neurons were tracked without error (Toyoshima et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to the original study.

claim: Nguyen et al. developed a method to track neurons in a freely moving worm, in which the deformation of the brain and the movements of neurons are considerably larger than those occurring in semi-immobilized worms.
source: To reveal the relationships between neuronal activities and animal behavior, Nguyen et al., developed a method to track neurons in a freely moving worm, in which the deformation of the brain and the movements of neurons are considerably larger than those occurring in semi-immobilized worms (Nguyen et al., 2016; Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to previous work.

claim: The method by Nguyen et al. for tracking neurons in freely moving worms requires a high-performance scientific computing cluster running on up to 200 cores simultaneously.
source: Although this method is powerful, it requires a high-performance scientific computing cluster running on up to 200 cores simultaneously.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a limitation of the previous method.

claim: 3DeeCellTracker segmented and tracked 113 cells in the initial 500 volumes from the worm #4 dataset.
source: With a few modifications (see Materials and methods), we used 3DeeCellTracker to segment and track 113 cells in the initial 500 volumes from the worm #4 dataset.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The images in worm #4 dataset were preprocessed by the straightening method, which is necessary for the current method.
source: Here we analyzed the images preprocessed by the straightening method (Nguyen et al., 2017), which is necessary for our current method.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation.

claim: In worm #4 dataset, many cell movements were comparable to the distances between cells, that is, RM ≥0.5.
source: Even after the straightening, the cell movements were quite large, with many comparable to the distances between cells, that is, RM ≥0.5 (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In worm #4 dataset, 90 cells were visually inspected while the remaining 23 were not checked because of difficulties arising from weak intensities/photobleaching and/or the cells being in dense regions.
source: We visually inspected the tracking of 90 cells while the remaining 23 were not checked because of difficulties arising from weak intensities/photobleaching and/or the cells being in dense regions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: In the original report of worm #4 dataset, 70 cells were inspected.
source: Note that 70 cells were inspected in the original report (Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation.

claim: In single mode, 66 out of 90 cells (73%) were correctly tracked without errors in worm #4 dataset.
source: We found that 66 out of 90 cells (73%) were correctly tracked without errors (Figure 6D–F, single mode), which is acceptable but not ideal.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In ensemble mode, multiple predictions of cell positions are made from different previous time points, and the final prediction is taken as the average of these predictions.
source: To further improve our method for the larger cell movements, we developed a new mode, in which multiple predictions of cell positions are made from different previous time points, and the final prediction is taken as the average of these predictions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a methodological innovation.

claim: In ensemble mode, 66 cells were correctly tracked without errors, and the remaining 24 cells were correctly tracked in most volumes (94%–98.2%) in worm #4 dataset.
source: When applying the ensemble mode, we again found 66 cells correctly tracked without errors, and that the remaining 24 cells were correctly tracked in most volumes (94%–98.2%).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The ensemble mode correctly tracked 44,905 out of 45,000 cell movements (99.8%) in worm #4 dataset, a result at least comparable to that in the original report.
source: In total, the ensemble mode correctly tracked 44,905 out of 45,000 cell movements (99.8%), a result at least comparable to that in the original report (Nguyen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to the original study.

claim: Large movements, including ones along the z-axis (across ~30 layers), occurred frequently in worm #4 dataset.
source: From the trajectories of two example cells, we found that large movements, including ones along the z-axis (across ~30 layers), occurred frequently (Figure 6G), demonstrating the excellent performance of our method on a desktop PC in this challenging dataset containing considerably large scale movements.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The ensemble mode requires longer times for the tracking than the single mode (10 versus 2 min/volume, respectively).
source: However, because the ensemble mode requires longer times for the tracking than the single mode (10 versus 2 min/volume, respectively), we used the single mode in the following analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The zebrafish dataset includes both large cells with stronger intensities that are easy to segment and small cells with weaker intensities that are difficult to segment.
source: This dataset includes both large cells with stronger intensities that are easy to segment and small cells with weaker intensities that are difficult to segment (Figure 7B, top and middle).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The photobleaching in the zebrafish dataset made it challenging to detect and track the weak intensity cells in the later part of the imaging.
source: The photobleaching in the dataset made it challenging to detect and track the weak intensity cells in the later part of the imaging, because of the substantial overlap between the small cell signals and background signals (Figure 7B; Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The weak intensity in the zebrafish dataset is unavoidable because of the extremely quick scanning rate of the SCAPE system (10,568 frames per second).
source: This weak intensity is unavoidable because of the extremely quick scanning rate of the system (10,568 frames per second).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an explanation for the weak intensity.

claim: The rapid beating of the zebrafish heart caused relatively large movements of all the cells in the x-y-z directions.
source: In addition, the rapid beating of the heart caused relatively large movements of all the cells in the x-y-z directions (Figure 7B, bottom; Figure 7—video 1; see below), making cell tracking more challenging than that for worm #1–3, which predominantly moved in the x-y plane.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: 98 cells were manually confirmed in the first volume of the zebrafish dataset.
source: After segmentation, we manually confirmed 98 cells in the first volume and tracked them automatically (Figure 7C and D; Figure 7—video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7.

claim: Among the 30 larger cells in the zebrafish dataset, 26 of them (87%) were correctly tracked in all 1000 volumes.
source: We found that among the 30 larger cells (size: 157–836 voxels) with higher intensities, 26 of them (87%) were correctly tracked in all 1000 volumes.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: When including smaller cells, 66 out of 98 cells (67%) were correctly tracked in the zebrafish dataset.
source: Even though the smaller cells with lower intensities were more difficult to track, when including them, we still correctly tracked 66 out of 98 cells (67%) (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7.

claim: The pipeline procedures for the zebrafish data were not optimized, except for a few parameter changes.
